q: Why can NOT IN return no rows at all?
a: If the subquery returns a NULL, x NOT IN (…, NULL) becomes x <> NULL = UNKNOWN for every row. Use NOT EXISTS or filter NULLs out of the subquery.

q: CTE vs subquery: which is faster?
a: Usually the same; most engines inline CTEs. CTEs win on readability and reuse within one query. For results reused across queries or very heavy steps, a temp table may be better.

q: What is a correlated subquery and when is it a problem?
a: A subquery that references the outer row, so it's logically re-run per row (e.g. compare salary to own department's average). It can be slow on large tables; a window function or a join to a pre-aggregated table usually replaces it.

q: What are recursive CTEs used for?
a: Hierarchies (org charts, category trees, bill of materials) and generating sequences such as a date spine to fill missing days. Anchor query + recursive part joined to the CTE, combined with UNION ALL.
EXISTS stops at the first match and is NULL-safe in the NOT form; IN compares against a list. Modern optimisers often plan them the same for the positive case, but prefer NOT EXISTS over NOT IN.
